economy.summary: His economic development plank proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and attracting employers who hire locally, saying young people should be able to build a good life without leaving Carbon County. He also proposes restricting institutional-investor ownership of single-family homes and penalties for homes left vacant and land-banked.
economy.short: Proposes reinvesting in trades, local hiring, limiting investor-owned homes.

taxes.summary: Supports full elimination of school property taxes, not rebates or freezes, replaced by a reformed broad-based consumption tax paired with a universal essentials credit, alongside pension reform; says Harrisburg has a spending problem and a discipline problem, not a revenue problem.
taxes.short: Supports eliminating school property taxes; proposes replacement consumption tax.

education.summary: Proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and vocational education so a young person can earn a good living without a four-year degree; this appears within his economic development plank, and his platform does not include a standalone education section.
education.short: Proposes reinvesting in skilled trades and vocational education.

healthcare.summary: Supports expanding nurse practitioner and physician assistant authority in underserved areas, treating telehealth and broadband as essential healthcare infrastructure, and protecting local clinics and hospitals; also proposes tax credits and certification-cost reimbursement to recruit and retain volunteer fire and EMS responders.
healthcare.short: Supports telehealth expansion, rural practitioner authority, protecting local hospitals.

guns.summary: His public safety plank says he will back local police, fire, and EMS with resources and training and defend the constitutional rights of Carbon County residents against efforts in Harrisburg to chip away at them; the platform does not detail specific firearms legislation. His campaign site lists a recommendation from Firearms Owners Against Crime, a gun-owner rights group.
guns.short: Pledges police support, defending constitutional rights; gun-rights group recommends.

economy.summary: In announcing his 2026 reelection bid, said he has sponsored legislation to lower housing costs and reduce regulatory burdens and has worked with state and federal officials to secure grants for communities across Carbon County.
economy.short: Sponsored bills to lower housing costs, reduce regulatory burdens.

taxes.summary: Pledged in his reelection announcement to continue fighting government waste, fraud and abuse and protecting taxpayers through fiscally responsible budgeting, citing his record of advancing property tax relief while opposing tax increases on families.
taxes.short: Pledges fiscally responsible budgeting, property tax relief; opposes tax increases.

abortion.summary: Voted for Senate Bill 106 of 2022, a proposed package of constitutional amendments that included language stating the Pennsylvania Constitution does not grant any right to abortion or to taxpayer funding of abortion; the measure passed the House 107-92.
abortion.short: Voted for no-constitutional-right-to-abortion amendment package in 2022.

education.summary: Said the November 2025 state budget invests in schools to ensure all students have access to a high-quality education through expanded school choice, scholarships for students in underperforming schools, and funding for the SHINE after-school program.
education.short: Supports expanded school choice, scholarships, after-school program funding.

healthcare.summary: As chairman of the House Human Services Committee, has led multiple hearings on Pennsylvania's drug crisis, focusing on fentanyl and xylazine dangers and the use of taxpayer dollars for recovery and related programs; this is committee work on the drug crisis rather than a stated broader healthcare platform.
healthcare.short: Leads drug-crisis hearings as Human Services Committee chairman.

energy.summary: Praised the November 2025 budget agreement for calling for Pennsylvania's exit from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, which he called job-killing and overly burdensome, saying the state can unleash Pennsylvania energy and that the agreement prevents a $2.5 billion energy tax, lowering utility costs.
energy.short: Supports exiting RGGI; says it prevents energy tax.

guns.summary: Voted against House Bill 714 of 2023, which would require background checks for private sales and transfers of long guns; the bill passed the House 109-92 in May 2023.
guns.short: Voted against expanding background checks to private long-gun sales.
